newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police probe bomb threats in capital.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police probe bomb threats in capital.

text.p: Police investigated bomb threats in Mexico City on Friday as leftist rebels denied they planned to attack civilians during weekend Independence Day celebrations.

Police and military officers examined one suspicious package left at the central Monument to the Revolution and took it away for further examination, witnesses said. A military officer told police the device contained a detonator but it was not clear if also contained explosives, a Reuter photographer at the scene said.

The device, left at the foot of the monumental arch on the capital's main Reforma boulevard, was about one foot (35 cm) long and contained wiring and tubing bound together with tape. Police sources said a warning about a second device had been received. No other details were immediately available.

Alongside the first device were found clippings from magazines, including pictures of starving African children, the late Latin American revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara and the German imperial eagle, witnesses said. German Chancellor Helmut Kohl is due to visit Mexico next week.
The Monument to the Revolution sits on a square between Mexico's main anti-narcotics agency headquarters and the Confederation of Mexican Workers trade union.

It consists of a raised dome originally built as part of a planned Congress building by turn-of-the-century dictator Porfirio Diaz. Construction was halted by the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution, in which Diaz was overthrown.
The incidents followed bomb threats in several cities in the last two weeks following attacks by the leftist Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) on army and police in several southern states.

The EPR, in a statement carried by newspapers on Friday, denied threatening to attack civilians during Independence Day celebrations in the capital's main Zocalo square on Sept. 15. It said a supposed EPR communique carrying the threats, published by newspapers on Thursday, was false and part of an effort by the government to discredit the group.

The EPR surfaced in June in the southern state of Guerrero and carried out bloody attacks there and in Oaxaca state on the night of Aug. 28 in which at least 14 people died. The goverment has declared the EPR a "terrorist" organisation and says it will pursue it with "all the force of the state."
